question: At unchanged home and away goal marginals, does learning how often both teams' chances rise or fall together improve first exact scores and three-score coverage?
population: Use each complete R5 domestic panel and R7 published fit, the contemporaneous R10 comparison rows and the subsequent unoverlapping November R11 extension. Use R14's frozen Understat match history. Evaluate the 2025/26 holdout, the 2026/27 recent slice and the November extension separately, retaining missing inputs. Prior results on these dates are known from earlier experiments. Only future registrations establish prospective performance.
identity: Use the R14 league, team aliases and strictly earlier match-calendar matching. Use at most eight prior domestic games per team, strictly before the target calendar day or the forward cutoff, whichever is earlier, and no more than 150 days before the target. For each source game use both sides' npxG and require nonnegative finite values, same-match identity, and mirrored npxGA agreement to within 0.001. Missing observations leave their original place in the eight-game window. No target npxG, goals or same-day update is allowed in a feature.
features: Design is [1, mean team concordance, mean team chance volume]. Within each club's eight-game window compute the Pearson correlation of its npxG for and against, and the mean of (for+against-2.6)/2 clipped to [-1,1]. Shrink each signal by n/(n+8). Correlation is zero with fewer than three usable pairs or zero variation. A missing side contributes zero. Arithmetic mean of the two clubs' shrunk signals. The intercept-only ablation fits the same data.
distribution: For the pregame home and away marginal pmfs p and q of the R7 grid, let u_i=2*(sum_{k<i}p_k+p_i/2)-1 and v_j analogously. The new joint pmf is p_i*q_j*(1+theta*u_i*v_j). This discrete Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copula preserves both goal marginals. Fit theta=0.95*tanh(X beta) per league by minimizing the summed negative log likelihood of observed score cells plus 2*sum(beta^2). Fit on chronological pregame anchor marginals before the validation season. Use L-BFGS-B with analytic gradient, zero start, coefficient bounds [-3,3]. For the ablation use only the intercept. No change based on test outcomes.
selection: Blend the original R7 joint grid and the alternative with a dose in {0,0.5,1}. Apply the existing R10 three-head validation procedure per league separately for contextual and intercept-only fits. Score head maximizes unique first hits then ordered-three hits then exact log score. Report full fixed doses and the two learned alternatives at the contextual doses as well. A zero-dose head inherits the signed original R7 pick.
comparisons: For every league and test slice publish four independent KPI hit/eligible counts, actual five-way total settlement, same-fixture gained/lost and date-clustered 95% net-rate intervals against R7, market and intercept-only. Include each dated fixture, the ordered predictions, likelihoods, historical exposure, per-league fitted coefficients and chosen doses. For research-only historical ranks use decreasing forecast probability of the issued first with kickoff then stable ID as tie breakers. Include all date batches, seat-level outcomes, batch sweeps and short coverage.
forward: Refit the dependence coefficients through the last completed target in each frozen R11 extension, keeping validation doses. Use original R5 prices and same-match R7 and market firsts. Register all still unstarted eligible fixtures in the five original R7 cohorts at a real UTC cutoff, retain each unique first, both ordered alternatives and its original batch seats before kickoff. Research forecasts and rankings remain distinct from comprehensive displayed choices. Use the original full R7 registered batch if it is still unstarted, otherwise record the time-bounded remaining slate and its original population explicitly. No automatic promotion.
